thread.title: Netflix Reports Earnings From Bear Market Territory

author: investopedia.com
title: Netflix Reports Earnings From Bear Market Territory
text:
Video streaming giant Netflix, Inc. ( NFLX ) offers internet content subscription services including movies and TV programming as well as DVD movies via mail. Netflix stock closed Monday at $333.13, up 73.5% year to date, but is in bear market territory at 21.3% below its all-time intraday high of $423.20 set on June 21.
Netflix is due to report quarterly earnings after the closing bell on Tuesday, Oct. 16, and analysts expect the streaming video giant to disclose earnings per share of 68 cents to 70 cents. A risk for Netflix is competitive products from Apple Inc. ( AAPL ) and Amazon.com, Inc. ( AMZN ). For Netflix, the critical factor is the cost of content versus growth in subscription revenue as its competitors offers their products.
Some analysts, including Citigroup, say that Netflix stock represents a " buy on the dip " opportunity given the company's strong portfolio of content that includes deals with stars such as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson. However, a respected market technician appearing on CNBC opined that Netflix stock was broken following its strong momentum run. Analysts from Goldman Sachs and Raymond James also chimed in with lowered price targets . Let's see what the charts have to say.
The daily chart for Netflix
Courtesy of MetaStock Xenith
Netflix has been above a " golden cross " since Oct. 12, 2016, when the stock closed at $99.50. A "golden cross" occurs when the 50-day simple moving average rises above the 200-day simple moving average and indicates that higher prices lie ahead. This signal led to the stock trading up to its all-time intraday high of $423.20 set on June 21. A negative reaction to earnings on July 16 is the price gap lower shown on July 17. The stock then moved sideways, staying above its semiannual value level of $291.84 and below its quarterly risky level at $396.87. These are two of the horizontal lines on the chart. Note how the stock is above its 200-day simple moving average at $326.78 as of Monday's close, which is a positive.
The weekly chart for Netflix
Courtesy of MetaStock Xenith
The weekly chart for Netflix is negative, with the stock below its five-week modified moving average of $350.79. The 12 x 3 x 3 weekly slow stochastic reading is projected to decline to 42.91 this week, down from 45.90 on Oct. 12. When the stock was trading at its all-time high of $423.20 during the week of June 22, the stochastic reading was 91.19, above 90.00 as an "inflating parabolic bubble," which proved to be an accurate technical warning.
Given these charts and analysis, traders should buy Netflix shares on weakness to my semiannual value level of $291.84 and reduce holdings on strength to my quarterly and monthly risky levels of $396.87 and $417.61, respectively.
